headline: High risk: Devin’s autonomous write/network capabilities can amplify caveman outputs into unsafe actions, while shared MCP and workspace surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman exposes files like CLAUDE.md and uses MCP; Devin also uses MCP and can read/write workspace files and act autonomously. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Devin ingests caveman-authored content from shared files or MCP outputs. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low because the shared channel is explicit.
conditions: IF Devin reads caveman-generated file content as instructions through a shared workspace or MCP server, injection is possible.
IF caveman writes prompt-like content into CLAUDE.md or docs consumed by Devin, hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and disable shared MCP endpoints.
Require provenance tags on any file Devin ingests.
Strip instruction-like text from caveman outputs before handoff.
Use a read-only export channel between agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Devin has broad network egress, cloud workspace files, and integrations that can transmit data to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion. If sensitive notes flow from caveman into Devin’s workspace, Devin can exfiltrate them through its default integrations. The shared-workspace path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF caveman stores secrets or private notes in files Devin can read, leakage becomes possible.
IF Devin is connected to GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion with real project data, those contents can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep sensitive caveman files out of Devin’s workspace.
Rotate or redact secrets before sharing artifacts.
Disable Devin integrations for the session.
Use separate OAuth principals for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on shared files and outbound APIs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run parallel sessions with shared integrations. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Because Devin’s defaults are autonomous and write-capable, the conflict is dangerous by default once co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository clone or cloud workspace, write conflicts can occur.
IF Devin commits while caveman edits the same files, git state can diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches.
Serialize write access with a lock file.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Review and merge changes manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman is a content-writing agent, so its outputs are likely to be treated as draft facts or instructions; Devin is an autonomous coding agent with shell, browser, and write permissions. If Devin consumes caveman output without verification, it can turn a mistaken draft into code changes, commits, or external messages. The downstream action authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Devin uses caveman output as authoritative input without a verification step, errors can cascade into actions.
IF caveman produces incorrect code or task instructions, Devin can operationalize them via shell or git.
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on caveman output.
Add a verification step that checks claims against source files.
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for handoffs from caveman.
Log and diff all generated actions before execution.
requires-engineering: implement structured handoff schemas with validation.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Devin handles repo clones, cloud workspace files, and writes to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion. That combination can move regulated or confidential project data into third-party SaaS integrations and cross-retention domains. No residency or retention controls are documented here, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF project notes or memory files contain regulated data, Devin’s integrations can propagate them to external services.
IF retention policies differ between caveman artifacts and Devin-connected SaaS, compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared artifacts.
Disable nonessential Devin integrations.
Redact logs and notes before transfer.
Confirm retention settings for each connected SaaS.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention across both agents.
